newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Sierra Leone rebels say they have sacked leader.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone rebels say they have sacked leader.

text.p: A senior member of Sierra Leone's rebel Revolutionary United Front (RUF) said on Saturday that the high command had sacked its leader Foday Sankoh for blocking the peace process.

Captain Philip Palmer, military representative on the RUF's external delegation, told Reuters that the decision was unanimous and had been made on Friday night after intensive radio contacts with rebel commanders and others in Sierra Leone.

He said Sankoh, who took up arms in 1991 and signed a peace deal with Sierra Leone's president in Ivory Coast on November 30, was effectively under house arrest in Nigeria's commercial capital Lagos, after travelling there on a private visit.

"With a view to promoting the spirit of healing and reconciliation and a rapid return to normalcy in Sierra Leone, the RUF High Command declares with immediate effect, the leadership role of corporal Foday Sankoh terminated," Palmer said in a written statement dated Saturday.
"For now we are trying to restructure the leadership to fill the vacuum," he told Reuters by telephone from the Ivorian town of Danane, near the border with Guinea and Liberia.

The statement, delivered to Reuters's office in Ivory Coast, denounced what it called Sankoh's "unyielding determination to thwart the peace process and prolong the suffering of the people of Sierra Leone".
